assumptions: Relative months from funded mobilization; activities are rolling windows, not fixed external deadlines.
First8weeks emphasize onboarding, relationship visits and product preparation; customer-facing workstreams overlap with deliberate waiting periods.

Prices, effort and rates are H35 authored planning inputs. Rates are loaded effective-person-week estimates including routine coordination; product costs add15percent delivery contingency. Delivery FTE reflects active effort; pool size rounds up at80percent project availability, rather than continuous full utilization.
Regional fixed resources exclude billable project delivery; project labor is counted only in direct costs.

Revenue from scope/pilot/production is planned at acceptance; support monthly. Direct delivery is expensed during implementation to expose working-capital pressure. Actual contract accounting may differ.
All discovery/pilot/production scopes are separately priced entitlements; no scoping credit in base. If credited, subtract the fee once and revise milestone receipts.
A6month slip shifts all project milestones, support starts and delivery costs; regional fixed costs continue. This is a stress case, not a probability or an inevitable regional cycle.
15percent regional reserves are funding allowances, not automatic P&L expense; liquidity buffer and reserve are not additive budgets.
Enterprise base excludes national-platform contracts, hardware, JV/equity capital, taxes, financing, FX and channel commissions. Add channel fees only where a paid channel arrangement is used.
Support is post-production service; amounts already bundled in implementation are excluded from the separate support line.
Production-template reuse permits more production scopes than newly completed pilots.
No fixed retail-style procurement lead time is asserted. Calendars follow counterpart availability, holidays and approval processes.
